skill.name: flow-nexus-platform
skill.description: Manage Flow Nexus authentication, hosted sandboxes, app deployment, billing, challenges, storage, and platform utilities through documented MCP workflows.
skill.summary: Operate Flow Nexus accounts, sandboxes, deployments, billing, challenges, storage, and monitoring from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: Flow Nexus

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and JavaScript template strings in documentation examples. The skill still carries real operational risk because it documents network-capable sandbox execution and sensitive Flow Nexus actions, including account upgrades, credit awards, tool-enabled assistant delegation, and remote code execution.

remediation.issue: Sensitive business operations are shown with user-controlled tier, amount, and user ID parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Require server-side authorization, role checks, idempotency, audit logging, and explicit user confirmation before upgrades or credit awards.

remediation.issue: Hosted sandboxes can execute arbitrary code, install packages, run startup scripts, and receive secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval for sandbox execution, isolate untrusted code, restrict outbound network access, and use scoped temporary secrets.

remediation.issue: The tool-enabled assistant can orchestrate agents and deploy code from conversation context.
remediation.suggestion: Default tool access to off, scope allowed actions, and request confirmation before any deployment, billing, or account operation.

remediation.issue: Examples include placeholder API keys and database URLs that users may replace with production secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Use secret-manager references in examples and warn users not to paste long-lived production credentials into prompts.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Sandbox Code and Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to create hosted sandboxes, pass environment variables, install packages, execute arbitrary code, and run startup scripts that install packages or clone repositories. This is an intended capability, but it can execute untrusted code and expose supplied secrets if used without confirmation and isolation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced examples directly show sandbox creation, environment variables, code execution, package installation, and git clone commands. The risk is contextual rather than hidden, so confidence is high.

semantic_findings.title: Business Logic Abuse Risk in Account and Credit Operations
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents calls that accept user-controlled account tiers, user IDs, credit amounts, reasons, and sources for upgrades and rewards. If Flow Nexus authorization is weak or an agent uses these calls without approval, users could alter entitlements or award credits improperly.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples expose sensitive business parameters directly, but the file does not show server-side authorization behavior. This supports high concern with some uncertainty.

semantic_findings.title: Tool-Enabled External Assistant Delegation
semantic_findings.description: The Seraphina assistant example enables tools and says the assistant can create swarms, orchestrate agents, deploy code, and retain conversation context. Delegating these actions to a remote assistant can cause unintended platform changes if prompts or history are untrusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example explicitly sets tool access to true and describes deployment and orchestration abilities. The impact depends on platform safeguards outside this skill.

content.value_statement: Teams need one place to control Flow Nexus accounts, sandboxes, deployments, credits, and challenges. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured prompts for those platform tasks.
actual_capabilities: Register, login, check status, reset passwords, and manage user profiles through Flow Nexus MCP commands.
Create and configure hosted sandboxes with templates, packages, environment variables, and startup scripts.
Run code in sandboxes, stream execution status, inspect logs, and retrieve generated files.
Search, publish, update, and deploy app store templates with metadata and analytics.
Manage credits, payment links, auto-refill settings, subscription tiers, and reward flows.
Use storage buckets, public URLs, realtime subscriptions, challenge submissions, leaderboards, and achievements.
limitations: It documents Flow Nexus MCP calls; it does not include an MCP server implementation.
Many examples use placeholder identifiers, secrets, URLs, and source code.
Administrative tools require Flow Nexus authorization that the skill cannot verify.
Sandbox execution can consume credits and may run untrusted code if used carelessly.

use_cases.title: Launch Development Sandboxes
use_cases.description: Create a hosted environment, add packages, set safe environment variables, run code, and inspect logs during development.

use_cases.title: Operate App Store Deployments
use_cases.description: Search templates, publish application metadata, deploy selected templates, and review analytics for Flow Nexus apps.

use_cases.title: Manage Credits and Challenges
use_cases.description: Check balances, configure payment flows, submit challenge solutions, and review achievements or leaderboards.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Flow Nexus Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Flow Nexus skill to check my authentication status, profile, credit balance, and recent account activity. Ask before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Safe Sandbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Flow Nexus sandbox for a Node API. Use placeholder secrets only, explain the template choice, and wait for approval before running code.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an App Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a suitable Flow Nexus backend template, list required variables, review security concerns, and draft a deployment plan for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Platform Operations
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Flow Nexus sandboxes, storage, app analytics, billing settings, and challenge activity. Identify cost, security, and cleanup actions.

output_examples.input: Create a beginner sandbox and explain the next steps.
output_examples.output: A concise setup plan that names the sandbox template, required packages, safe placeholder variables, expected credit impact, and approval checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Review my app store deployment readiness.
output_examples.output: A deployment checklist covering metadata, versioning, tests, license, documentation, template variables, and risks that need owner approval.

output_examples.input: Summarize my Flow Nexus account activity.
output_examples.output: A plain-language account summary with authentication status, balance, recent payments, active sandboxes, storage use, and challenge progress.

best_practices: Confirm account, billing, and credit changes with the user before calling Flow Nexus tools.
Use short-lived, least-privilege secrets when configuring sandboxes or deployments.
Delete unused sandboxes and storage objects after testing to control cost and exposure.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production database URLs or API keys into examples or shared prompts.
Do not enable tool-using assistant actions without reviewing the planned operations.
Do not publish app templates without tests, license details, and security notes.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It documents Flow Nexus workflows for users, sandboxes, deployments, billing, challenges, storage, realtime events, and system utilities.

faq.question: Does the skill include working Flow Nexus credentials?
faq.answer: No. The examples use placeholders, and users must provide authorized credentials through approved Flow Nexus flows.

faq.question: Can it run code?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes Flow Nexus sandbox execution, so users should approve commands and avoid untrusted code.

faq.question: Can it change billing or credits?
faq.answer: It documents payment links, auto-refill, tiers, balances, and rewards. Confirm every billing or credit action before execution.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should teams review before use?
faq.answer: Review authorization, sandbox isolation, outbound network policy, secret handling, and approval rules for account or billing actions.
